name: SM_Burn_Hole_C_PR

textures.channels: base colour sRGB + alpha (cover, dithered by the pit material)
tangent normal, OpenGL (green up; flip green on import)
R occlusion, G roughness, B void mask of the pit material (not metallic)

material_exception: unique BC/N/ORM bakes private to this asset (not a row of ART_STANDARD.md section 2): remains are one-off set pieces
pivot: bbox centre in X/Y, lowest point at z = 0; in Blender +X is screen right and +Y screen up (north) for a yaw_from_sprite row
dresses: two holes burnt through the floor, run together (picture 3)
known_weaknesses: A flat alpha-tested card 6 mm above the floor with modelled splinters and charcoal lumps on it: nothing is cut out of the floor itself. The depth (the cut face of the far side, the dark below) is drawn by the `pit` material of the kit importer from the view direction; it assumes one depth for the whole hole, and its far face has no texture of its own. The scorch fades by a per-frame dither (needs temporal anti-aliasing to look soft). The Blender renders show the flat sheet without that shader.
derived_from: tools/gore_sheets.py pit_sheet (numpy and PIL, no scan)
